real_conflicts: The proposal to 'break the symmetry' by shifting the title to the left or right side of the upper negative space is rejected. This would result in a standard, unbalanced layout that fails to utilize the strong central perspective of the road. The title must remain centered to act as the 'sky' or 'ceiling' of the composition, reinforcing the architectural weight of the town.
accepted: The proposal to introduce a subtle SVG noise filter (film grain) over the background is accepted. This texture will allow the typography to integrate with the image rather than floating on top of a sterile digital gradient, adding the necessary cinematic tactility.
concession: I concede that the current serif font is too light and the tracking is too wide, making the title feel like a placeholder. I also concede that the tagline is currently illegible and visually weak.
compromise: Instead of moving the title off-center, we will tighten the tracking and increase the weight of the title to anchor the top of the poster. We will then move the tagline 'Some places disappear twice' off the central axis—positioning it slightly to the right or left of the vanishing point—so it does not block the viewer's eye from traveling down the road, while maintaining the overall centered hierarchy.
nonnegotiable: The typography must be treated as a structural element of the landscape, not a label. The title must visually 'cap' the horizon line or align with the perspective of the road to create a unified composition.
